findings.title: Reminders with empty message or missing sendTo are never counted as failures and will retry forever
findings.body: The retry logic only increments retryCount when `twilio.scheduleSMS` returns falsy or when an exception is thrown. But if `message` is empty or `sendTo` is null (e.g., an SMS_NUMBER step with no sendTo, or a booking with no smsReminderNumber, or a template that produces an empty message), the code skips the entire `if (message?.length && ... && sendTo)` block without incrementing retryCount. Such a reminder stays `scheduled: false` with retryCount 0 and is re-fetched by the cron job on every run until its scheduledDate passes — exactly the infinite rescheduling this PR is meant to fix, and the most common cause (missing/invalid phone number often means sendTo is absent, not a Twilio failure).

findings.title: Catch block increments retryCount even when the SMS was successfully scheduled in Twilio
findings.body: The try block covers both the Twilio call and the follow-up `prisma.workflowReminder.update` that marks the reminder scheduled. If Twilio scheduling succeeds but the database update fails (transient DB error), the catch handler increments retryCount while leaving `scheduled: false`. The next cron run will schedule the same SMS again in Twilio (duplicate message to the attendee), and after two such occurrences the reminder is deleted while a Twilio-scheduled SMS still exists. The retry increment should only happen when the send itself failed, or the success-path update should be in its own try/catch.

findings.title: retryCount-based deletion in deleteMany is not scoped to SMS method or unscheduled reminders
findings.body: The new OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` deletes WorkflowReminder rows of any method (EMAIL, WHATSAPP) and any scheduled state, unlike the first branch which is constrained to `method: SMS`. Today only this SMS cron increments retryCount so the impact is latent, but the schema field is on the shared WorkflowReminder model — as soon as any other code path (e.g., the parallel scheduleEmailReminders cron or WhatsApp scheduling) uses retryCount, this job will silently delete those reminders, including ones already successfully scheduled with a Twilio referenceId. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` (and arguably `scheduled: false`) to the retry-count deletion clause.
